nodes.name: Pt SA synthesis with Cl ligand
nodes.procedure: Pt single atoms anchored on RuOₓ-covered Ru nanoparticles (Ru-NPs@RuOₓ) with Cl ligands (Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ) were synthesized using Cl-containing Pt precursor through spontaneous deposition method (detailed procedure provided in Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: We have synthesized the Pt SAs anchored on the surface of RuOₓ-covered Ru NPs (Ru-NPs@RuOₓ) with and without the addition of Cl ligands (denoted as Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ and Pt₁/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ, detailed nomenclature in the Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Pt SA synthesis without Cl ligand
nodes.procedure: Pt single atoms anchored on RuOₓ-covered Ru nanoparticles (Ru-NPs@RuOₓ) without Cl ligands (Pt₁/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ) were synthesized using Cl-free Pt precursor through spontaneous deposition method (detailed procedure provided in Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: For a comparison, we also synthesized the Pt SAs on Ru NPs@RuOₓ (Pt₁/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ) using Cl-free precursor.

nodes.description: Acidic HER performance in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ (LSV)
nodes.source_text: The acidic HER performance of Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ was evaluated in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ ... exhibits an initial HER overpotential (η) of 92 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², such an overpotential decreases during the HER process and finally approaches a stable value of 13.2 mV ... The Tafel slope ... is approximately 56.8 mV dec⁻¹ ... The calculated exchange current density (j₀) ... is ca. 5.7 mA cm⁻² ... Its mass activity (MA) at an overpotential of 50 mV ... reaches 15.3 A mg_Pt⁻¹ ... the calculated turnover frequency ... at -0.05 V on Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru -NPs@RuOₓ is 15.1 H₂ s⁻¹

The steady-state polarization curves ... show that the MEA with Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ achieves superior electrolysis performance, delivering a cell voltage of ∼1.66 V at 1.0 A cm⁻² and ∼1.76 V at 2 A cm⁻² ... with an ultralow Pt loading of 10 μg_Pt cm⁻² ... exhibits outstanding stability ... with a decay rate of only 17.8 μV h⁻¹ at 1.0 A cm⁻² over 1000 h

A durability comparison ... indicates that Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ exhibits the smallest MA loss after 24 h electrolysis ... During the early stage of the HER (0.5∼3 h) Pt₁Cl₀.₅ / Ru - NPs@RuOₓ catalyst experiences only a 7.2% decay in MA

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show uniform dispersion of Ru-NPs with average diameter of ca. 2 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images (Figures S1 and S2) show the uniform dispersion of Ru-NPs with an average diameter of ca. 2 nm.

properties.description: Higher magnification inset showing detailed nanostructure with diffraction pattern

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings demonstrate homogeneous dispersion of Pt and Cl elements on the Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mappings (Figure S1b) further demonstrate the homogeneous dispersion of Pt and Cl elements on the Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-STEM confirms presence of isolated Pt single atoms on Ru-NPs with FFT showing Ru crystal facets (100), (101), and (002).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inset fast Fourier transform (FFT, inset in Figure 1a) analysis derived from aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-STEM) image (Figures 1a and S3) of Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ exhibits three crystal facets of metallic Ru, corresponding to (100), (101), and (002), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns verify metallic Ru NP bulk structure with crystal facets (100), (101), and (002).
nodes.evidence_snippet: which is also verified by X-ray diffraction patterns (Figure S4), confirming that the bulk structure is the metallic Ru NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Cl 2p identifies Pt-Cl ligand (Cl_Pt 2p3/2 at ~198.4 eV) and Ru-influenced Cl (Cl_Ru 2p3/2 at ~197.5 eV); O 1s shows RuOx at ~530 eV; Ru 3d3/2 shifts ~0.3 eV due to Cl electronic modulation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution XPS analysis of the Cl2p (Figure 1e) identifies two distinct Cl species: one corresponds to conventional Pt-Cl ligand (ClPt 2p3/2 at ~198.4 eV), and another is influenced by Ru (ClRu 2p3/2 at ~197.5 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determines Pt mass loading of ca. 5.31 wt% for Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ and 4.76 wt% for Pt₁/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ (Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry determines that the mass loading of Pt is ca. 5.31 wt% (Table S1) within Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs catalyst. This catalyst exhibits a comparable Pt mass loading of ca. 4.76 wt% (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Pt-Cl bending vibration at 185 cm⁻¹ for Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ, absent in Cl-free catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra (Figure 1c) shows an obvious vibration peak (Pt-Cl) at 185 cm⁻¹, assigned to Pt-Cl bending vibration, distinct from vibration peak (Ru-Cl).

nodes.characterization_summary: IR confirms Pt-Cl stretching vibration at 318 cm⁻¹ for Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Infrared spectroscopy (Figure 1d) confirms the existence of Pt-Cl stretching vibration peak at 318 cm⁻¹ for the Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ, consistent with reference standards.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge XANES shows white-line energy lower than PtO₂ indicating Pt valence below +4; Ru K-edge shows negative white line shift indicating partial Ru reduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The normalized X-ray adsorption near-edge spectra (XANES, Figure 1f) indicate that the white-line energy feature at the Pt L₃-edge of the Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ is slightly lower than that of PtO₂, demonstrating the Pt valence state below +4.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge EXAFS shows Pt-O at 1.99 Å, no Pt-Pt; second-shell fitting reveals Pt-ClPt (R≈2.604 Å, N=0.9) and Pt-ClRu (R≈3.337 Å, N=1.6).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transforms (FTs) of extended Xray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra (Figure 1g) exhibit a dominant peak near 1.67 Å (with a fitted value of 1.99 Å) corresponding to the Pt-O interatomic distance.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Pt L₃-edge XANES during HER shows Pt valence decrease from 2.5 to -0.3 over 2000 s at -0.05 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the in situ normalized Pt L₃ edge XANES spectra (Figure 3a-c) reveal the valence states of Pt decrease from 2.5 to -0.3 over 2000 s HER at a constant potential of -0.05 V versus RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ EXAFS during HER shows Pt-O diminishes, Pt-Ru emerges and intensifies (CN from 2 to 5), Pt-Cl stabilizes at CN≈0.5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From in situ EXAFS (Figure 3d), at open circuit potential (OCP), only Pt-O coordination is detected... Upon applying a reductive potential of -0.05 V, the Pt-O signal diminishes within 2000 s.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows Ru-O reduction and enhanced Pt-Cl bending vibration at ~190 cm⁻¹ with Stark effect as potential decreases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the potential decreases from 0.7 to 0 V, the Ru-O bond is gradually reduced, and the bending vibration peak of Pt-Cl near 190 cm⁻¹ becomes more pronounced, accompanied by a weak Stark effect.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-HER AC-STEM shows adjacent Pt atoms confirming Pt-Cl-Pt motif formation; Pt₁/Ru-NPs@RuOₓ shows Pt aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: AC-STEM image (Figure S3) of the Pt₁Cl₀.₅/Ru-NPs@RuOx sample after the HER shows the adjacent Pt atoms, indirectly proving the possible formation of Pt-Cl-Pt motif.
